text:
alex: Quick heads-up — the Console p95/p99 view has a smoothing window (5m) and when route-tagging is on we’re seeing p99 spikes disappear in the per-endpoint breakdown. Anyone else noticed this?

maria: I noticed weird flattening on /v1/generate yesterday around 14:03 UTC. thought it was sampling.

alex: Yeah, looks like we smooth the percentile timeseries after we rollup by route. That means different route mixes get averaged together and the p99 disappears. :thinking:

jen: Wait — are we applying smoothing to raw latency samples or to the percentile values themselves? Big difference.

alex: To the percentile values (we compute p50/p95/p99 per minute, then apply an EMA over those points for the chart).

sam: That rings alarm bells — EMA on percentiles is not statistically sound. It can hide spikes and produce misleading stability. We should either smooth histograms / tdigest inputs or do no smoothing for tail percentiles.

maria: Agreed. UX folks wanted smoother lines to avoid noisy graphs during demos. But smoothing the percentile scalar is probably the wrong tradeoff for p99. For p50 maybe ok.

jen: Proposal: keep a default smoothing for p50 and p95, but disable smoothing for p99 in per-endpoint breakdowns and when route_tag != "global". Also add a toggle in the Console: "Show raw p99 (no smoothing)".

alex: +1. Also a telemetry nuance: currently we merge requests with different payload_size buckets before computing minute percentiles. If heavy requests end up in the same minute as many light ones, tail is dominated by low-latency requests. We should compute percentiles per payload_size bucket, then rollup with weighted merge, or at least expose "by-payload" slice.

sam: Right — two separate problems: (1) histogram/tdigest merge policy pre-minute-aggregation, (2) smoothing post-aggregation. Fixing both will give correct attribution for endpoint breakdowns and routing policies.

maria: How much effort to change UI? We need a small toggle + explanation blurb. Backend change to compute per-bucket tdigests may be heavier.

jen: Backend notes: storing minute-level tdigest per route/payload_bucket is straightforward but increases cardinality. We can limit buckets to [small, medium, large] and default to disabled unless "detailed telemetry" is on for the project.

alex: For immediate mitigation: 1) remove EMA from p99 charts in endpoint breakdowns, 2) surface sample counts prominently next to percentile values, 3) add a banner: "Smoothing may hide tail spikes; toggle raw p99". Then plan tdigest rollup in next sprint.

sam: Also consider routing-policy effects: when we route to fallback model variants, latency distribution changes. The console should show a route-weighted p99 and also the p99 per-variant to avoid the merged view hiding the fallback's tail.

maria: Good call — we already have variant weights in the rollout UI. We can reuse that to generate per-variant percentiles. UX: add small caret to expand variant breakdown under the endpoint row.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-21T14:15:23Z — feature/console-telemetry-toggle rolled to staging (sha abc123). :rocket:

alex: Nice, can we patch the staging Console to disable p99 smoothing in endpoint view immediately so SRE can validate?

jen: I'll open a short-lived feature flag: console.disable_p99_smoothing_endpoint_view. If QA + SRE signoff we can flip prod. Ticket created: https://tracker.internal/PLAT-8123 (summary: "Disable p99 smoothing in endpoint breakdown; surface raw p99 and sample count").

sam: For the longer term, I'll draft an RFC on histogram-first aggregation + sample-bucket rollups (will include cardinality & cost estimates).

maria: Can someone add a short note in the Console docs about how percentiles are computed and when smoothing applies? Customers keep asking.

alex: I'll write the docs blurb and link the RFC once ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

jen: action items -> jen: feature flag + patch, sam: RFC, alex: docs + QA checklist, maria: small UX toggle copy.

sam: one more thought — quotas and alerting: our alert rules that reference p95/p99 may be affected by smoothing. If we change smoothing semantics, we should run a quick audit of alerts to avoid firing noise.

maria: noted. I'll add alert-audit to the staging checklist.

alex: ok closing this thread for now; follow-ups in PLAT-8123 and the RFC. Ping me if you need help with test data (I can generate mixed-payload traces).
